title: GraphQL Exercises
description: Read each example in its lesson first. Predict the result, then check your answer. The notes explain the idea and one common mistake.

exercises.question: A schema names allowed fields. The resolver supplies a value for greeting. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The Query type declares greeting. The root resolver supplies its string when that field is selected. A query can only ask for fields declared in the schema.

exercises.question: The query picks title and leaves out pages. The resolver still holds both fields. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The query asks for title only. GraphQL reads that field from the resolved book and leaves pages out. GraphQL object fields need a selection of their inner fields.

exercises.question: An argument supplies a value to a field. The resolver receives it in an object. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The argument object gives n value 4. The resolver returns the product 8. The input must match the argument type.

exercises.question: A variable lets one query be reused with different values. Its value is supplied separately. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The separate variable object provides n. GraphQL inserts that value into the field argument. A declared required variable must be supplied.

exercises.question: Square brackets describe a list type. The query selects title for each book. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The resolver returns two book objects. GraphQL reads title from each one. The list item shape must match the schema type.

exercises.question: Aliases name two uses of the same field so both results can appear together. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: small and big are response aliases. Their different inputs produce 4 and 8. Two different arguments on one field need distinct response names.

exercises.question: A fragment gives a group of fields a name. The query spreads that group onto a Book. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The fragment supplies title and pages selections for Book. Both fields appear in the result. A fragment has to apply to the type at that position.

exercises.question: An enum limits a value to named choices. GREEN is a schema label, not arbitrary text. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The resolver returns GREEN, which is a legal enum value. JSON represents the enum name as text. The resolver result must match an enum value.

exercises.question: A mutation names a write action. This local example changes one in-memory score. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The mutation resolver receives 8, stores it in the local score and returns the new value. The resolver must implement the change; declaring a mutation alone does not save data.

exercises.question: The exclamation mark means a field must not be null. This resolver breaks that rule, so GraphQL reports an error. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The resolver returns null for a field marked non-null. GraphQL reports the schema-rule failure. Use non-null only when the resolver can honour that promise.
options: Cannot return null for non-nullable field Query.name.

exercises.question: The include directive can choose whether a field is requested. The flag is false here. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The include flag is false, so pages is skipped even though its resolver exists. The directive input is Boolean, not the text "true" or "false".

exercises.question: An input type groups values sent into a mutation. It is separate from an output object type. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The mutation receives a BookInput object. Reading book.title gives Moon Trip. This example returns the title only; a real resolver needs storage to save a book.
